All nine cited pins reproduce, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head, artifact and version are both 1, and file08StatusToken is the bare string OPEN matching the live DR-G16 status cell. That token attack has extra force on this subject, because a neighbouring row's join is cited throughout and its standing could easily have leaked in; it did not, and the registerRowNote states that each join holds its own row's token. The three named classes are identical four ways — live G16 v2, the catalog, the join's top-level field and the copy inside its authoring obligation — and match the semicolon-separated members of the live file 08 harness cell. The hardest thing to get right here is the two-join structure. monorepo-leftover-join.v2 is the DR-121 row join and already carries OBL-G16-HARNESS-SPEC, OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-G16-EXECUTION, which this gate join carries too. It is disclosed four times and precisely, including by naming both shared leftovers in the monorepo role — 'OBL-G16-FX-AUTHORING and OBL-CI-ENCODING-RESERVED remain leftover-design on that row. This file is not that join and does not retarget those leftovers.' I verified monorepo v2 at source: DR-121, token OPEN, both obligations still leftoverDesign true. Both artifacts hold the shared obligation open, so nothing closes on one row while appearing closed on the other, and the CI-encoding leftover is held by a guard obligation at rides-DR-121 rather than taken. The completeness probe produced five candidate omissions and none survived. Two, OBL-1 and OBL-7, were my own false positives from a greedy identifier pattern and I disclose them because the raw extraction looked like two missing obligations. The three real ones — OBL-G13-RESERVED, OBL-MATRIX-CORPUS, OBL-THRESHOLDS — sit in a single field of G16 v2, dr118Split, which places them as DR-118 leftover-design. Carrying them here would be the same theft the dispatch forbids for the CI encodings and would additionally require naming G13, which the dispatch forbids outright, so omitting them is correct. The EE-7e standing the join reports matches monorepo v2's OBL-EE-7E exactly, and DR-117 leftover-design is not closed. Bookkeeping reconciles at five and five. One disclosure: all three Claude-lane verdicts this join rests on are my lane's and one is unmistakably mine — the g16 catalog verdict at 39df3652, whose two advisories I wrote. The join cites it as ACCEPT 0/0, which is correct under the corpus convention that 0/0 counts blockers and SHOULD-FIX, as with the v14 contract's ACCEPT 0/0 carrying ADV-1; I checked that against corpus usage rather than against my memory of my own verdict. The DR-G16 harness cell still reads 'not authored' while G16 v2 exists — the tenth row in that condition, covered by my standing recommendation to dispose of the family in one act.
